summary: The TICKET Act requires primary and secondary ticket sellers to clearly display the total ticket price upfront, itemize fees before purchase, and ban the practice of selling tickets they do not actually possess. It also restricts misleading domain names or claims of official affiliation, sets mandatory refund or replacement policies for canceled or postponed events, and requires the Federal Trade Commission to enforce these rules and report on enforcement of the Better Online Ticket Sales Act of 2016.

affected_groups.effect: Will see total ticket prices upfront, receive itemized fee lists, benefit from clear cancellation and refund rules, and experience fewer misleading representations regarding ticket availability and official affiliations.

Must update pricing displays to show total costs upfront, itemize fees, cease speculative ticketing practices, comply with restrictions on domain names and affiliation claims, and follow mandated refund or replacement policies.
affected_groups.group: Ticket Issuers and Secondary Market Sellers

affected_groups.effect: Must enforce the requirements of the act under FTC Act authorities and submit a report to Congress on the enforcement of the Better Online Ticket Sales Act of 2016.

key_provisions: Requires ticket issuers, secondary market sellers, and exchanges to clearly and conspicuously display the total ticket price in all advertisements, marketing, or price lists and at the very beginning of the purchasing process.
Mandates an itemized breakdown of the base ticket price and all individual fees before a customer completes a ticket purchase.

Prohibits sellers and exchanges from selling, offering, or advertising tickets they do not actually or constructively possess, while carving out specific rules for services that help customers obtain tickets.
Bans ticket resellers from falsely claiming official affiliation or endorsement by a venue, team, or artist, and prohibits unauthorized use of venue names in web domains and URLs.
Establishes refund and replacement requirements for canceled or postponed events, including full refunds for canceled events and specific options for events postponed for more than six months.
Directs the Federal Trade Commission to submit a report to Congress regarding the enforcement of the Better Online Ticket Sales Act of 2016 within six months of enactment.
Treats violations of the act as unfair or deceptive acts or practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act, giving the FTC enforcement authority.
missing_information: Specific dollar penalty amounts for violations of the act.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The TICKET Act requires primary and secondary ticket sellers to clearly display the total ticket price upfront, itemize fees before purchase, and ban the practice of selling tickets they do not actually possess. It also restricts misleading domain names or claims of official affiliation, sets mandatory refund or replacement policies for canceled or postponed events, and requires the Federal Trade Commission to enforce these rules and report on enforcement of the Better Online Ticket Sales Act of 2016.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation introduces nationwide transparency requirements for the ticketing industry by banning hidden fees and speculative ticket sales while establishing standardized refund policies. Its impact covers the entire commercial ticketing sector for public events in venues holding over 200 people, enforced by the Federal Trade Commission.
